title: Grade 2 Science — Mon, Jun 23
description: Animals and Their Young Ones — Day 1 of 5: Viviparous vs Oviparous animals
subject: science

questions.question: Which animal gives birth to live young ones (does NOT lay eggs)?
questions.explanation: Dogs give birth to live young ones (puppies). Hens, frogs and lizards lay eggs.

questions.question: Which animal lays eggs?
questions.explanation: Hens lay eggs. Cows, goats and cats give birth to live young ones.

questions.question: Animals that give birth to live young ones are called:
questions.explanation: Viviparous animals give birth to live young ones. The word comes from 'vivus' (alive) and 'parere' (to give birth).

questions.question: Animals that lay eggs are called:
questions.explanation: Oviparous animals lay eggs. Birds, fish, reptiles and most insects are oviparous.

questions.question: A butterfly is an example of which type of animal?
questions.explanation: Butterflies lay eggs — they are oviparous. The eggs hatch into caterpillars which then become butterflies.

questions.question: Which of the following is a viviparous animal?
questions.explanation: Whales are viviparous — they give birth to live young ones in the ocean. Crocodiles, parrots and turtles lay eggs.

questions.question: A duck lays eggs. A rabbit gives birth to babies. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Duck is viviparous; rabbit is oviparous
Duck is oviparous; rabbit is viviparous
questions.explanation: A duck lays eggs so it is oviparous. A rabbit gives birth to live young ones so it is viviparous.

questions.question: Which of these is the ODD ONE OUT (does not belong to the same group)?
questions.explanation: Dogs, cats and cows are viviparous (give birth to live young ones). Eagles lay eggs, so they are oviparous — the odd one out.

questions.question: Fish are oviparous. What does this mean?
options: They give birth to live young ones
questions.explanation: Oviparous means egg-laying. Most fish are oviparous and lay eggs in water.

questions.question: Snakes lay eggs. Which group do they belong to?
questions.explanation: Since snakes lay eggs, they are oviparous. Most reptiles like snakes, lizards and crocodiles are oviparous.

questions.question: Which pair shows one oviparous and one viviparous animal?
questions.explanation: Hen is oviparous (lays eggs). Dog is viviparous (gives birth to puppies). So 'Hen and dog' is the correct pair.

questions.question: All mammals are viviparous. Which of these is NOT a mammal?
questions.explanation: Lizards are reptiles, not mammals. They are oviparous (lay eggs). Elephants, bats and deer are mammals and viviparous.

questions.question: A platypus is a mammal that lays eggs. What makes it special?
options: It is the only flying mammal
It is a mammal that is also oviparous
It gives birth like all other mammals
questions.explanation: The platypus is unique — it is a mammal (has fur, feeds young with milk) but also lays eggs, making it oviparous. It is one of very few egg-laying mammals.

questions.question: A child is making two groups: Group A = viviparous, Group B = oviparous. Where does a shark go?
questions.explanation: Interestingly, some sharks lay eggs (oviparous) and some give birth to live young (viviparous). This is a fascinating exception in nature.

questions.question: Why is it useful for scientists to classify animals as viviparous or oviparous?
options: To count how many animals exist
To understand how different animals reproduce and care for offspring
To find out what animals eat
To measure how big animals grow
questions.explanation: Classifying animals helps scientists study their reproductive methods. Viviparous animals carry young inside; oviparous animals protect eggs outside. This affects how they care for offspring.
